claim: the entry's id is stable across runs and is the trace tag
why: src/sim.jl:2528-2533 the id is assigned at admission, monotonic, and named in the handle's who "device $id (Type)"; src/roster.jl:414-415 _writer_schemas tags the trace by that name; probe K089 schemas "device 1 (Pad)" => [:elevator, :throttle]. Entries persist across runs until detach!.

claim: replay feeds the same batches to the same drain
why: src/sim.jl:2665-2666 the drain point substitutes the feed under :replay. src/sim.jl:2706-2740 _replay_drain! applies the recording's records through compiled scatters at the same frame-top position, in the same order, through the ordinary loop. The conversion back is done once, up front, in _compile_feed (trace.jl:85-104), as the doc's line 180 says.

claim: Staging cells and the published reference are release/acquire @atomic fields
why: src/dataplane.jl:25-27 StagingCell `@atomic pending::Union{Nothing,Base.RefValue{B}}` (one pointer word); src/dataplane.jl:594-596 Published `@atomic latest`. Published is accessed :release/:acquire (src/sim.jl:2797, 2856). The staging cell's CAS and swap (src/dataplane.jl:463-465, 492) use Julia's default sequentially consistent order, which includes release/acquire.

claim: The roster is a plain immutable value
why: src/sim.jl:1645: append!(roster, plane.roster) reads the roster once into a run-local vector the loop uses. src/roster.jl:254 RosterEntry is an immutable struct, and the plane's vector changes only at the stopped-sim gate. Probe P6: ismutabletype(RosterEntry) is false. | plane.roster is a mutable Vector rebuilt at each attach!/detach! (roster.jl:450-455), and each entry's WriterAccount is mutated by the loop. The configuration the spec lists (entries, claims, order) is fixed for the run, so the text holds in substance.

claim: On an operator interrupt the wrapper makes no should_abort consultation
why: src/devices.jl:654-659. The InterruptException branch forwards _request_stop!(…, :interrupt) and files no report. The finally line `entry.should_abort && stop!(entry.handle)` (src/devices.jl:671) still runs, but it changes nothing because the stop word keeps its first issuer (src/control.jl:82). Probe P9 (probe.jl:72) attaches with should_abort = true and ends with ControlRequestedStop(:interrupt). | Read literally, the code does still evaluate should_abort, and the code comment calls that consult 'inert'. The doc's claim holds in effect.

claim: The device tasks write `MalformedDatum`, and the writers list names where each diagnostic is written (device cell side)
why: src/devices.jl:401-403 report!(handle, ::MalformedDatum) writes the handle's own diag_cell, and MalformedDatum is the one kind it takes. Probe: a device that reports from its loop shows totals.malformed == 1 in its own record ('device 1 (Reporter)').

src/control.jl:180 writes DebtReanchor into loop_diag, reached from the loop's _advance! at sim.jl:2109. src/sim.jl:1572 writes UnboundedRun into sim.plane.loop_diag at run! entry, on the loop's task. Probe: a DebtReanchor reported into loop_diag shows in the 'loop' record.
